contentText: Ten years after Islamic State (IS) group terrorists staged Belgium’s deadliest attack in peacetime, killing 32 people and wounding more than 300, authorities vow to have learnt the right security lessons. Since the 2016 massacre, a coordinated extremist profile database has been set up, and the number of state security staff has been heavily increased. But some victims say their psychological and physical traumas have not yet been properly recognised.
